correctness.rationale: For primitive differences modulo p², expansion t=a+pz gives a p-fold root-of-unity sum supported only on roots of u+3va²=0 modulo p. There are zero, one or two such roots; since p² is odd, one term is nonzero and two p²-th roots cannot cancel, proving the derivative-root criterion. For differences divisible by p, the prime-level p-term sum vanishes precisely when Ut+Vt³ permutes F_p; horizontal nonzero U is allowed, and a pure cubic is additionally allowed only for p≡2 (mod 3). The quadratic-character sum argument excludes mixed nonzero U,V for p≥5. Thus no primitive vertical differences, at most p reduction classes, and each residue fibre has at most p compatible frequencies, forcing p saturated fibres. Their reduced graph uses at most (p+1)/2 allowed directions; by the Rédei–Megyesi theorem a noncollinear p-set needs (p+3)/2, hence it is an affine graph with allowed slope. Every saturated fibre is exactly one horizontal or (when permitted) vertical affine line, giving the distinct count p(p+1)/2·[p(1+1_{p≡2 mod 3})]^p. All endpoints p≥5 and labeling conventions checked.
